items.title: A finite birational morphism of integral schemes with normal target is an isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the standard normality criterion in the relative form: a finite (or merely integral) birational morphism f : X -> Y of integral schemes with Y normal is an isomorphism (statement lines 14629-14633). The proof is short but not a citation: it has to move to an affine open V of Y whose inverse image U is affine, which is where quasi-affineness of a finite morphism is used, and then work with the ring map O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) (proof lines 14636-14639). The decisive move is to place both rings inside the same fraction field and observe that normality of Y makes O_Y(V) integrally closed there, while integrality of f puts every element of O_X(U) into that integral closure, so equality follows (proof lines 14640-14643). This is H2: the reduction to affine data and the integral-closure comparison are the non-formal content, but no Noetherian hypothesis and no descent argument are needed and the whole argument occupies a single paragraph.
